sonselasuchus:study:1.title: Osteology and relationships of a new shuvosaurid (Pseudosuchia, Poposauroidea) from the Upper Triassic Chinle Formation of Petrified Forest National Park, Arizona, U.S.A. (Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology, 2025)

facts.statement: Sonselasuchus fossils were found in the Chinle Formation of Arizona, United States, dating to the Late Triassic (Norian age).
facts.quote: It is known from the Late Triassic (Norian age) Chinle Formation of Arizona, United States.

facts.statement: All known Sonselasuchus fossils come from the Kaye Quarry, discovered by Tom Kaye in 2014.
facts.quote: The Sonselasuchus fossil material is all known from the Kaye Quarry (locality PFV 410)—named for Tom Kaye, who discovered it in 2014

facts.statement: Over 950 disarticulated bones belonging to at least 36 individuals were collected from the Kaye Quarry.
facts.quote: More than 950 disarticulated and non-associated (not in anatomical position) bones referable to a shuvosaurid were collected from the Kaye Quarry, together belonging to at least 36 individual animals.

facts.statement: Sonselasuchus was described as a new genus and species by Elliott Armour Smith and Christian A. Sidor in 2026.
facts.quote: In 2026, Elliott Armour Smith and Christian A. Sidor described Sonselasuchus cedrus as a new genus and species of shuvosaurid pseudosuchian

facts.statement: Sonselasuchus possessed a bipedal posture, an enlarged pubic boot, large eye sockets, and toothless jaws.
facts.quote: These traits include a bipedal posture, enlarged pubic boot, large orbits, and edentulous (toothless) jaws.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the snout of Sonselasuchus may have had a keratinous beak similar to turtles and birds.
facts.quote: The snout may have borne a keratinous rhamphotheca (beak), similar to turtles, birds, and some non-avian dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Sonselasuchus was quadrupedal as an immature animal but shifted to bipedalism as it grew older.
facts.quote: They determined that there was likely a negative allometric trajectory of the forelimb dimensions relative to the hindlimb. This would indicate a shift in the mode of locomotion; the animal would be quadrupedal when immature, shifting to bipedalism at a later ontogenetic stage.

facts.statement: Sonselasuchus is classified as a member of the superfamily Poposauroidea and the family Shuvosauridae.
facts.quote: A member of Poposauroidea belonging to the family Shuvosauridae.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Sonselasuchus in the Shuvosauridae clade in an unresolved relationship with Effigia and Shuvosaurus.
facts.quote: This dataset recovered Sonselasuchus as a member of the poposauroid clade Shuvosauridae, in an unresolved polytomy including Effigia and Shuvosaurus

facts.statement: Sonselasuchus lived during the Norian stage of the Late Triassic, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus name Sonselasuchus is derived from the Sonsela Buttes on the Navajo Nation in Arizona.
facts.quote: The generic name, Sonselasuchus, referencing the geologic member of the Chinle Formation from which it is known, in turn derived from the Sonsela Buttes on the Navajo Nation in Arizona.

rejected.statement: Sonselasuchus is an extinct genus of poposauroid pseudosuchian, a group of crocodile-line reptiles, within the family Shuvosauridae.
rejected.quote: Sonselasuchus is an extinct genus of poposauroid pseudosuchian (crocodile-line reptile) in the family Shuvosauridae.
